_description: Task13 DRIFT field, FINE transcription -- the 0.0925mm grid used for BOTH the near-field solve and the final stitched volume. The coarse sibling (example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_task13_coarse.json) is the 0.37mm far-field grid. SPACINGS ARE 0.37 / 0.0925, NOT 0.4 / 0.1: the pitch is pixelSize + pixelGap = 2.2 + 1.5 = 3.7mm, and 3.7 = 37 x 0.1 with 37 prime, so NO coarse spacing that is both an integer multiple of 0.1mm and an exact divisor of 3.7mm exists apart from 0.1 and 3.7 themselves. Solving pitch = n * fine and coarse = 4 * fine with 4 dividing n gives n = 40: fine 3.7/40 = 0.0925mm, coarse 3.7/10 = 0.37mm, still the validated 4:1 ratio. hybrid_iterate.py _cells() requires the transverse extent to be a WHOLE number of cells and raises otherwise, so this is a hard constraint, not a preference. PAD/GAP SPLIT IS NOW THE SAME IN BOTH FILES -- 2.2 / 1.5 here and in the coarse file. The two files used to carry different splits because neither divided both spacings; at 0.37/0.0925 the same split quantizes identically on both grids, so the coarse and fine solves model the SAME 2.22mm pad: 2.2/0.0925 -> 24 cells and 2.2/0.37 -> 6 cells are both 2.22mm, 1.5/0.0925 -> 16 cells and 1.5/0.37 -> 4 cells are both 1.48mm, and 24 + 16 = 40 = 4 * (6 + 4) is exactly the transverse node count on each grid. If you retarget the pitch, re-derive the spacings first -- a split that quantizes differently on the two grids makes the far field and the near field disagree about the pad, which --domain no will NOT catch. CATHODE FORMULA, so the value can be recomputed by hand when the drift length or the bulk field changes: CathodePotential = -BulkField * (driftZDepth - pixelPlaneLowEdgePosition). The drift length is 159.9 - 10.0 = 149.9mm, so this file's -8400 V is 56.04 V/mm nominal. The value is maintained BY HAND on purpose, so the bulk field stays a visible, editable number rather than a derived one. DEPTH: driftZDepth 159.9 is the electron launch node; the cathode sits on the domain's last plane at ceil(159.9/0.37) = 433 coarse cells = 160.21mm, which is 1732 fine cells exactly (433 x 4), so both grids close on the same physical cathode. TILE SIZE: Npixels 9, i.e. a 9x9 pad tile at the 3.7mm pitch = 33.3mm transverse for the weighting probe; the DRIFT field is one periodic tile, so Npixels does not size this file's domain. CHAMFER: chamfer_r 0.5 quantizes to 5 cells = 0.4625mm at this spacing -- the closest available to 0.5, since 6 cells would be 0.555mm. It was exactly 0.5 at the retired 0.1mm spacing, so this is a real 0.0375mm change to the pad chamfer footprint, which is the feature that drives gap-centre drift overshoot; expect the overshoot metric to move slightly against earlier 0.1mm runs. THIS file's chamfer is the one that matters -- the pad and its chamfer live inside the near field. GridPotential does NOT enter the cathode calculation: the shield grid has holes and is transparent at the tile centre, so it is not an equipotential plane terminating the field -- on the earlier 149.9mm/-7500 V run, measured phi at the grid plane z=11.6mm was about -71 V, nothing like GridPotential. The bulk field is set by the CATHODE against the PIXEL PLANE at 0 V. GridPotential instead sets the collection field between the grid and the pads.
